claims.statement: The transcription request chain runs AppController.transcribe → BackendPort.transcribe → the start_transcription Tauri command → Application::transcribe, with progress traveling as out-of-band job events while only the final TranscriptionResult is returned through the IPC promise.

The webview mints the transcription jobId with crypto.randomUUID() before invoking so the first worker event already belongs to this job, and the job-event subscription is established in AppController.start() before any action can run (subscribe-before-invoke).

Speaker-hint validation happens before the job slot is claimed: validate_speaker_hint rejects a zero exact count and zero-bound or inverted ranges as INVALID_SPEAKER_HINT before any workspace access, pinned by invalid_hint_is_rejected_before_workspace_access observing zero prepare_job calls.

run_transcription enforces a readiness gate after the claim: it loads the saved EnginePreset, re-diagnoses, and fails with SETUP_REQUIRED unless engine_ready, models_ready, and ffmpeg_ready all hold, so no meeting folder or worker process is created for an unprepared engine.

JobRegistry::claim_with_id holds one active-job Option: a second claim is refused BUSY and a job id that already has registered artifacts is refused JOB_ID_CONFLICT; the returned JobGuard releases the slot on Drop so an early error, cancelled future, or panic cannot leak the slot (pinned by failed_transcription_releases_active_job).

prepare_job_directory validates the input as a regular file (INVALID_AUDIO), canonicalizes the output root, creates the meeting folder with the adoption rule (an input inside {stem}/ reuses that folder; others get a deduplicated fresh {stem}) and seeds the newest sibling <stem>.aligned.v2.json into the fresh folder, leaving the engine-tag check to whichever engine runs.

Application::asr_context builds AsrContext {terms, names, aliases} from the saved glossary terms plus the full participant roster (names and spoken aliases — the attendee selection governs refinement, not transcription); when all three lists are empty the context is None and no context is sent, both pinned by transcription_carries_glossary_and_roster_for_asr_biasing and transcription_sends_no_asr_context_without_saved_context.

AsrContext::into_wire_json serializes the {terms, names, aliases} JSON shape the worker's parse_asr_context reads; the adapter hands it to the worker through a temporary galpi-asr-context-{job_id} file created with mode 0600 and create_new (never via argv) and removes it after the run regardless of outcome.

The worker is spawned per preset on one call shape: Qwen3 runs the candidate stack's own engine/qwen3/.venv python and WhisperX the pinned engine/.venv python, with --engine plus optional --asr-context, --num-speakers, or --speaker-range, from the worker root as cwd; the preset defaults to Qwen3 and follows the saved preset (transcription_defaults_to_qwen3_and_follows_the_saved_preset).

Transcription runs in a scrubbed environment from process_environment (app-cache HF_HOME/TORCH_HOME, Korean locale, telemetry off, pinned uv dirs) with no HF_TOKEN because only the prepared cache is needed; Qwen3 additionally forces HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 and TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 so no network round trip can occur mid-meeting.

run_process starts the child in its own Unix process group with null stdin and kill_on_drop, wrapped in an armed ProcessGroupGuard whose Drop sends SIGKILL to the group, so a dropped future can never orphan the model stack.

Worker stdout is the protocol: each line must parse as a version-1 envelope (else WORKER_PROTOCOL_ERROR), Completed/Refined events are captured once as the run's completion carrier (a second completion is a protocol error), and every parsed event is re-emitted to the webview as it arrives.

Worker stderr is batched logging — flushed at 100 ms or 32 lines — with the last 20 lines retained so a non-zero exit reports PROCESS_FAILED carrying the worker's own final diagnostic; lines are read through a 64 KiB bounded reader that fails rather than growing unbounded.

The worker redirects stdout to stderr during a run so dependency chatter cannot corrupt the protocol, and every abnormal exit still reaches the host as one error event — InvalidInput as INVALID_INPUT with exit 2, any other exception as ENGINE_ERROR with exit 1 — emitted by a lock-serialized, versioned, monotonic-sequence EventWriter.

engine.transcribe dispatches on --engine between the Qwen3 and WhisperX pipelines; both converge on the same ending — filter degenerate segments, write <stem>.srt and <stem>_화자별.txt atomically, and emit one completed event with srt, txt, checkpoint, segments, and filtered.

The WhisperX pipeline runs large-v3-turbo on CPU (int8, ko, VAD 0.6/0.4) with hotword biasing packed from terms→names→aliases under a 200-character budget, aligns and diarizes on MPS with automatic CPU retry, and treats a checkpoint as reusable only when its engine tag is whisperx or absent — skipping only transcribe and align, since diarization, filtering, and publication always re-run.

The Qwen3 pipeline decodes any input through the bundled ffmpeg to 16 kHz mono WAV, plans ~25 s chunks capped at 30 s cut at ffmpeg silencedetect midpoints (staying under mlx-qwen3-asr's own re-split limit), runs the MLX 8-bit session per chunk with language Korean, timestamps, and a freeform bias context built from the ASR-context file and hard-capped at the 500-character BIAS_CONTEXT_CHAR_BUDGET.

Qwen3 checkpoints raw aligner word spans in <stem>.aligned.v2.json and reads one back only when the engine tag is exactly qwen3 (the other engine's file is re-transcribed over, pinned by test_checkpoint_round_trips_and_rejects_the_other_engine); diarization uses pyannote community-1's exclusive speaker variant on MPS with CPU retry and the speaker hint as num_speakers or min/max_speakers, and group_word_spans breaks segments at terminal punctuation, a speaker change, a 0.8 s pause, or a 12 s limit.

Worker filtering drops known hallucination phrases plus token-dominance repetition loops and repeated-phrase loops by coverage thresholds, and filter_segments additionally drops tail-noise segments after a ≥120 s silence past the audio midpoint; the kept/filtered counts ride the completed event and surface as the result summary.

TauriEvents forwards each worker event to the webview as a job-event payload of jobId plus the flattened camelCase event, matching the Zod rawJobEventSchema; toJobEvent demotes an unrecognized payload into a frontend-stream log line instead of throwing, because a throw inside Tauri's callback would make a host/window mismatch vanish silently.

reduceJobEvent's load-bearing rules are: events with a foreign jobId are ignored, settled statuses drop further phase events, percent is monotonic within a phase via Math.max (new phases adopt their own value), logs are split and capped at 200 lines, and completed settles the job at phase writing and 100%.

The worker's phase vocabulary (transcribing, aligning, diarizing, writing) drives the transcription panel's waveform rail: phaseState ranks the phase list against the phaseOrder array, marking earlier phases complete, the current one current, and later ones pending.

On completion the adapter contain-checks the returned srt/txt/checkpoint paths under the canonicalized job folder (WORKER_PROTOCOL_ERROR if outside), maps an empty checkpoint string to None, and run_transcription registers the Artifacts under the job id — the registration that later makes open_artifact and reveal_output work — before renderResult shows the artifact rows, the counts summary, and hides the checkpoint row when absent.

On failure the worker's error event sets status failed with the cause in the error slot while the message slot keeps the stable "작업이 실패했습니다." line; the subsequent IPC rejection re-applies the same state through failJob without duplicating the announcement, and the JobGuard drop has already freed the slot for the next attempt.

Cancellation escalates through signals: JobRegistry::cancel (JOB_NOT_FOUND, ALREADY_CANCELLING, or JOB_FINISHED) fires the oneshot; terminate_on_cancel sends SIGTERM, waits 3 s, then SIGKILLs the whole process group and reaps the child, returning CANCELLED; the UI applies cancelJob immediately on the click and failJob no-ops on an already-cancelled state, so cancellation is announced once as a decision rather than a failure.
